statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. NQ made a new overnight high near 29,168 and immediately gave it back, which removes the one amplifier flagged an hour ago. Two independent quotes put NQ at 29,111.00 and 29,116.25, up 5.25 to 10.50 points or roughly 0.03% on the 29,105.75 settle, inside a 29,017.00-29,168.25 band spanning about 0.52%. The KOSPI sits at 6,530.06, down 2.49%, after traversing 6,408.82 to 6,601.92 in both directions; the Nikkei 225 is at 64,971.28, down 0.85%, mid-way between 64,609.47 and 65,279.63. Monday's US close left the Nasdaq Composite down 0.76% and the S&P 500 down 0.28% on a semiconductor de-rating that took the Philadelphia index down more than 3%. VIX settled at 15.85 within a 15.61-16.06 range, the 10-year yield is 4.72% and the 2-year 4.26%, both up under 3bp, and WTI is 85.38 with Brent at 92.34. Tail eases to 9 in the low band because every market carrying the impulse has retraced part of it. Stress is 46 in the elevated band on the breadth of the chip de-rating ahead of Wednesday's Core PCE, GDP and Nvidia stack.
recommendation: Descriptive only. The decisive observation this hour is a failed extension. NQ pushed to a new overnight high near 29,168, roughly 13 points above the band top an hour ago, and has since faded about 55 points back to the middle of its range rather than holding the extreme. Holding near a session extreme is one of the amplifiers this measure watches for, and that condition has now cleared. Seoul shows the same shape at larger amplitude: down as much as 4.3%, back up to 6,601.92, and now at 6,530.06, a market oscillating inside a wide band rather than trending through it. None of the remaining amplifiers is present: there is no reopen gap, no repeated extension after failed pullbacks, the overnight range spans about half a percent, and yields, VIX and oil are all moving in fractions rather than confirming a directional impulse. Tail therefore sits well below the block threshold, and the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON with a green status for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The flagged danger window spans 13:30Z-14:30Z, covering the US cash open and the 14:00Z Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and Richmond Fed cluster. Every forecast hour maps to EA_ON because the conditional Tail path peaks at 18, below the watch band. Confidence is 85: the futures level, range and settle are confirmed by two independent quote sources, the Asian levels, yields, oil and calendar are all verified, and the single deduction is a conflicting delayed VIX quote resolved in favour of the 15.85 settle.
headline: NQ makes a new overnight high near 29,168 and fades it back to 29,111-29,116, clearing the session-extreme amplifier; Tail eases to 9 with Stress at 46 into Wednesday's Core PCE and Nvidia stack
body:
The observation that moves the assessment this hour is a failed extension. An hour ago NQ was trading 29,133 to 29,142 in the upper part of a 29,017.00 to 29,155.50 band, and holding near a session extreme was explicitly flagged as the one amplifier present. Since then the contract pushed to a new overnight high of 29,167.75 to 29,168.25 and has given back roughly 55 points, trading 29,111.00 on Investing.com and 29,116.25 on Yahoo Finance, up 5.25 to 10.50 points or about 0.03% on the 29,105.75 settle. The band is now 29,017.00 to 29,168.25, about 151 points or 0.52%. NQ sits close to the middle of it. An extension that fails and reverts is the direct opposite of the repeated-extension-after-failed-retracement structure this measure targets, and the amplifier flagged an hour ago has cleared.

Asia shows the same pattern at much larger amplitude. The KOSPI opened 2.4% lower, fell to 6,408.82 for a decline near 4.3% against the 6,696.96 close, recovered as far as 6,601.92, and now trades 6,530.06, down 2.49%. That is a full traverse of a roughly 3% band in both directions inside one session. The Nikkei 225 is at 64,971.28, down 0.85%, sitting between a 64,609.47 low and a 65,279.63 high. Neither index is pinned at its extreme. The underlying impulse is real and named: Monday's US session produced a semiconductor de-rating with the Philadelphia index down more than 3%, Micron off more than 5%, Sandisk and Western Digital both down over 5% and Nvidia down close to 3%, and the shared Finviz context shows all seven tracked semiconductor names lower with a mean decline near 3%. South Korea carries an idiosyncratic overlay as well, with the SK Hynix union rejecting a tentative wage deal on a 50.08% no vote.

What the cross-asset set does not show is confirmation. The 10-year yield is 4.72% and the 2-year 4.26%, both up under 3bp, and the 30-year is 5.24%. VIX settled at 15.85 inside a 15.61 to 16.06 range and the delayed volatility futures reading is marginally softer overnight; a conflicting delayed cash quote near 14.89 was set aside in favour of the settle confirmed by a second source. WTI at 85.38 and Brent at 92.34 are up 0.44% and 0.19% following the new US sanctions programme aimed at Iran's trading partners, a live geopolitical channel but one currently priced in fractions rather than as a discontinuity. Monday's megacap tape was a rotation rather than a broad de-risking: Meta, Amazon, Google and Microsoft all closed higher while Nvidia, Broadcom and Tesla fell, leaving five of eight positive with dispersion above two percentage points.

Stress stays elevated at 46 rather than falling with Tail. The chip de-rating is broad, Seoul is swinging several percent intraday, and the two-day catalyst stack is close: Core PCE, the second estimate of Q2 GDP and durable goods all print at 12:30Z on Wednesday, with Nvidia's results after that session's close. Today's own calendar is medium-impact throughout, with Barkin at 12:00Z, Case-Shiller at 13:00Z, the Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and Richmond Fed cluster at 14:00Z and the two-year auction at 17:00Z. The danger window is drawn narrowly around 13:30Z to 14:30Z, covering the cash open and that stacked release, because that is where the evidence points rather than across the whole session. Confidence is 85 on two agreeing futures sources, verified Asian levels and ranges, verified yields, oil and calendar, and fresh cross-asset context, with a single deduction for the conflicting VIX quote.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. The window opened at 03:00Z on 24 August with Tail 7 and Stress 38 in a normal mode and held a 7-12 band through the Asian hours. The first structural peak came at 07:00Z, where the European open produced Tail 19 and Stress 58 in a trend-down mode; it faded to 17 within an hour and to 12 by 09:00Z. The window's only non-green slots surrounded the US cash open: Tail 20 with Stress 54 in an event/whipsaw mode at 13:00Z mapped to WATCH, and the single peak at 14:00Z reached Tail 26 with Stress 60 in a trend-down mode, mapping to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. That structure did not persist. From 15:00Z onward Tail collapsed to 13 and then held a 7-10 band for the remainder of the US session while Stress decayed from 54 to 42, the signature of a rotation whose directional efficiency faded rather than a path that denied mean reversion. The window closed with Tail 12 at 00:00Z, 9 at 01:00Z and 10 at 02:00Z on 25 August in a mixed mode, while Asian cash indices sold off sharply and then recovered a substantial part of the move. The full 24-hour range is Tail 7 to 26 and Stress 38 to 60, and 22 of the 24 slots mapped to EA_ON.
outlookSummary: The conditional path stays inside the low Tail band for all 24 hours, so every slot maps to EA_ON. It opens at 9 on the observed failed extension and the cross-market retracement, holds a 10-11 band through the Asian afternoon and the cash closes, then lifts to 14 at 07:00Z for the European cash open - the same window that produced yesterday's first structural peak before fading it within an hour. The series eases through the European morning to a floor of 11 by 10:00Z, lifts to 12 for the 12:00Z Barkin and ADP checkpoints, and reaches 16 at 13:00Z as the US pre-open, the Case-Shiller release and the 13:30Z cash open open the flagged danger window. The horizon peak of 18 falls at 14:00Z, where the first full US cash hour overlaps the Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and Richmond Fed cluster; that hour also carries the horizon's conditional Stress peak of 56 and, together with 13:00Z, the only event/whipsaw modes in the forecast. Conditional Tail then decays to 15 and 13 through the afternoon, holds 12-13 across the two-year auction and the closing rotation, and reaches its horizon floor of 10 during the 21:00Z CME maintenance halt when no continuous price path can form. It lifts to 11 at the reopen and settles at 12 across the Asian opens on Core PCE and Nvidia day, where conditional Stress firms to 51 and conditional Confidence tapers to 78 as evidence quality thins at the far end of the horizon.
